title: Telemetry-based cost & latency attribution pipeline (route/model/customer chargeback)
creator: Alyssa Patel
description: Goal: build a robust, streaming-first pipeline that attributes per-request cost and latency down to route/model/customer dimensions so the Console can show accurate chargeback and SLA-level breakdowns. Scope includes: event ingestion from Console backend and inference runtime, enrichment with model metadata and customer pricing tiers, an attribution engine that handles shared-token batching and KV-cache savings estimation, and storage/aggregation tiers for near-real-time dashboards and daily billing exports. Non-goals: replacing invoicing system or changing pricing math in this iteration. Success metrics: median latency for queryable breakdowns < 5s for 95th percentile, end-to-end data freshness < 60s for streaming views, accuracy vs offline ground truth within 2%, and monthly cost reports matching billing exports within 0.5% after reconciliation. High-level design: 1) Produce canonical telemetry events at the Console API layer (request_id, route_id, model_variant, tokens_requested/generated, kv_cache_hit_fraction, batch_id, timestamp, customer_id). 2) Stream into Kafka topic telemetry.events. 3) Enrichment Flink/beam job joins model catalog (model size, quantization profile) and pricing table; performs per-request attribution heuristics for batched requests and shared KV savings; emits attributed events. 4) Real-time aggregators write to ClickHouse for fine-grained, high-cardinality query patterns powering Console charts and alerts. 5) Daily materialized rollups and exports to the billing warehouse for invoicing and historical analysis. Attribution nuances: - For batches, split generation tokens across constituent requests proportional to pre-generation prefix length and configured priority weights. Allow configurable fallback to equal split for ambiguous cases. - KV-cache savings: use a hybrid estimator: exact KV-hit fractions when runtime emits them, otherwise heuristic based on sequence_prefix_similarity and cache TTL windows. - Model variant equivalence: map model variants to cost classes (e.g., gpt-large-8bit ~ base-large) to simplify per-token cost grouping. Rollout plan: start with opt-in telemetry for 10% of traffic, validate accuracy against offline Spark job, expand to 100% and switch Console to new endpoints. Backfill approach: run offline attribution job to populate historical 90 days into ClickHouse before enabling UI. Monitoring and SLOs: pipeline lag, producer failure, enrichment join drift, and ClickHouse write errors instrumented to PagerDuty. Data retention: raw telemetry kept 90 days, aggregates 2 years. Privacy/compliance: strip PII at source, config-driven customer opt-out.
